observation_summary: The system throws a NullPointerException or NoSuchMethodError when attempting to call a real method on an interface mock. The tests expect a MockitoException to be thrown instead, indicating that the system fails to validate whether the target of the call is an interface before attempting to invoke the real method.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by the absence of a guard condition that checks if the object being mocked is an interface. When `callRealMethod()` is invoked on an interface, the system proceeds with an invalid operation (attempting to call a real method on an interface which has no implementation), leading to runtime exceptions. Adding a check to validate the type of the mock before proceeding is a classic 'Checking' defect.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the capability to handle interfaces is missing, the fix is a local validation check (guard) rather than a design-level overhaul of the mocking framework's architecture.
The issue is not an incorrect implementation of an algorithm, but rather the failure to validate the input (the mock type) before executing the method call.
